title: Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding
author: Ellis Brown, Chris Hoang, Shengyi Qian, Shang-Wen Li et al.

summary: How multimodal language models should encode visual input remains up for debate. Most models use a pretrained vision encoder, while some recent recipes train the encoder from scratch with the language model or remove it entirely.
takeaways: Because published models also differ in data, architecture, and compute, comparing them cannot isolate the effect of each choice.

We disentangle these choices via a controlled framework where we pretrain all models from scratch on common data and compare them on visual question answering and language benchmarks at matched lifetime compute.
These results also hold across backbone sizes, when encoder pretraining is treated as free, and when starting from a pretrained language model.
